strokeOrder: draw the short stroke from its top down and to the right
lift, begin at the upper right and sweep down to the left past the end of the short stroke, then without lifting curve round and run out to the right along the base
lift, draw the left tick of the dakuten down to the right
lift, draw the right tick down to the right
strokeOrderNote: KanjiVG's 03069 file records ど as four stroke paths in this order and direction: と's two strokes (the short slanting stroke and the long curve), then the dakuten's two ticks, the left one first, each drawn down to the right; so there are three pen lifts.

strokeOrderSource.citation: KanjiVG, kanji/03069.svg, hiragana ど (U+3069 HIRAGANA LETTER DO), four stroke paths kvg:03069-s1 to s4 (Ulrich Apel and contributors, CC BY-SA 3.0)
strokeOrderSource.variation: KanjiVG stores each stroke as one directed path in writing order: s1 to s2 are と's strokes, the same paths as in its file for と, kanji/03068.svg; s3 and s4 are the dakuten, the left tick first and then the right one, each drawn down to the right. Only the order and direction are taken from that file. The learner path's coordinates are the bundled Noto Sans JP outline's own medial line, so the print glyph's proportions, not KanjiVG's handwriting-style ones, decide where each stroke runs. In KanjiVG and in the print glyph alike, the short stroke ends on the long one, so the two strokes touch.

notes: と voiced, read do. The end of いちど, once, in もう いちど, once more.
